![Laricobius nigrinus feeding on adelges tsugae](https://blogs.cornell.edu/nyshemlockinitiative/files/2018/06/20170406_160045-29m8060.jpg)


This insect is one of the main resources used to control the hemlock woolly adelgid. Adelgids are tiny invasive insects with that are putting the hemlock trees in check. Their voracious feeding behaviuor is capable of whiping out tress of 4-10 years old, and they have no natural enemy in Eastern North America.

Becuase of that the "Lari" insect have been introduced from the pacific northwest as a desperate measure to stop adelgid invasion and preserve natural forest.
